Supreme Court of India Announces Recruitment for 20 Court Master (Shorthand) Posts: Dates, Eligibility, and Pay Scale

29 Oct 2026, 01:29 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Careers Desk · Source: www.freejobalert.com

The Recruitment Cell of the Supreme Court of India has issued an official notification inviting online applications for the direct recruitment of Court Master (Shorthand) positions within its Registry. A total of 20 tentative vacancies have been announced, though the final count remains subject to change based on administrative requirements.

Online registration for these positions opens on 25 October 2026 and will continue until 15 November 2026 at 11:55 p.m. Interested and eligible candidates must submit their applications through the official website.

Eligibility Criteria and Service Requirements

To qualify for the Court Master (Shorthand) role, applicants must meet specific educational, technical, and professional experience benchmarks:

  • Educational Qualification: A Bachelor's degree from a recognized university.
  • Technical Proficiency: English shorthand speed of 120 words per minute (w.p.m.) and computer typing speed of 40 w.p.m.
  • Experience: A minimum of 5 years of regular service experience in the cadre of Private Secretary, Senior Personal Assistant, Personal Assistant, or Senior Stenographer in government departments, Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs), or statutory bodies.

Applicants must also adhere to the prescribed age limits. As of 1 October 2026, candidates must not be below 30 years of age, and the upper age limit is set at 45 years, subject to applicable rules.

Salary and Pay Structure

Candidates selected for the Court Master (Shorthand) posts will be placed at Level 11 of the Pay Matrix. The pay scale ranges from Rs. 67,700 to Rs. 2,08,700, with an initial basic pay of Rs. 67,700, in addition to eligible allowances.

Selection Process and Exam Pattern

The multi-stage selection process comprises:

  • Objective Type Test
  • Shorthand (English) Test
  • Typing Speed Test on Computer
  • Interview

According to the examination guidelines, the Objective Type Test will not feature negative marking. Minimum qualifying marks have been established for each phase, requiring 50 marks out of 100 for the objective test, 50 marks out of 100 for the shorthand test, 10 marks out of 20 for the computer typing test, and 15 marks out of 30 for the interview.

How to Apply

Eligible candidates can complete the application process by following these steps:

  • Visit the official Supreme Court of India website at [www.sci.gov.in](https://www.sci.gov.in) and access the recruitment portal.
  • Complete the online registration and fill out the form with necessary personal and educational details.
  • Upload scanned copies of required documents, including photographs, signatures, academic certificates, experience proofs, and caste or community certificates if applicable.
  • Pay the non-refundable application fee via the online UCO Bank payment gateway.
  • Save the application number and print a copy of the submitted form for future reference.

Practical Implications and Verification

What is Confirmed

  • Vacancy Count: Exactly 20 tentative vacancies have been notified under notification number F.6/11/CM(S)/2026-SC (RC).
  • Key Dates: Online applications run from 25 October 2026 to 15 November 2026.
  • Pay Scale: Level 11 of the Pay Matrix (Rs. 67,700 - Rs. 2,08,700).

What is Unknown

  • Exact examination dates and venue allocations have not been announced in the initial notification and will be communicated later via the official portal.

How to Check the Original Announcement

Readers can verify all details, read the complete notification text, and track future updates directly by visiting the official website of the Supreme Court of India at [www.sci.gov.in](https://www.sci.gov.in).
